title: Panettone: Orange and Raisin Enriched Sweet Bread
summary: A soft, buttery enriched bread full of orange-soaked raisins and candied peel, baked tall and golden.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Plump the raisins
steps.text: Warm the raisins with the orange juice until steaming, then cover and leave for 15 min so they soften and do not draw moisture from the dough.

steps.title: Mix the liquids
steps.text: Whisk the warm milk, golden syrup, egg, yolks, vanilla and orange zest in the jug.

steps.title: Start the dough
steps.text: Combine the flour, yeast and salt in the mixer bowl. With the dough hook running on medium-low, pour in the liquids and knead for 3-5 min until no dry flour is left.

steps.title: Work in the butter
steps.text: Add the soft butter one piece at a time, then knead on medium-high for about 10 min. The dough is ready when it pulls away from the sides but still clings at the base; adding the fat after the gluten has formed keeps the bread light. On low speed, mix in the peel and raisins with any juice for 2 min.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Knead briefly on a floured surface, form a tight ball and set it in the greased bowl. Cover and leave at warm room temperature for about 2 h, until doubled.

steps.title: Shape and prove
steps.text: Pat the dough into a 30 cm round, fold the edges into the middle, then flip it and tighten into a smooth ball. Place it seam side down in the tin, cover and prove for 2-2.5 h until the top is about 5 cm above the rim.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan). Brush the top with beaten egg and bake for 15-20 min until golden, then turn the tin, cover loosely with foil and bake 30-40 min more, until the centre reads 88 °C. The foil stops the sugary crust from burning while the inside finishes.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Leave in the tin for 15 min, then turn out and cool on the rack for about 3 h before slicing, so the crumb sets.

tips: A common mistake is adding the butter too early; wait until the dough has formed, then add it slowly.
Proving can take longer in a cool kitchen, so judge by height, not time.
Use a thermometer: enriched dough can look done outside before the centre is cooked.
Stale slices make excellent bread and butter pudding.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Wrap well and keep at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze slices for up to 2 months. Toast or warm gently to serve.
